test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2022: Official Paper (Held On: 16 March, 2023 Shift 4)
subject: general
question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

To breast the tape
solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 4'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"To breast the tape" **is an idiomatic expression originating from competitive running.
 
• In a race, **a tape is stretched **across the finish line.
 
• The first person to break this tape with their chest, or** "breast the tape," is the winner. **(दौड़ में जीतना)
 
• So, it essentially **means** "To win a race".

Therefore, the **correct answer** is: *'To win a race'.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **To shut someone’s mouth **- This phrase generally means to cause someone to stop speaking, often by making them feel guilty or embarrassed. It does not have a similar meaning to "To breast the tape". (किसी का मूंह बंद करना).
 
• **To create problems** - This phrase means to cause difficulties or obstacles. (समस्याएँ पैदा करना).
 
• **To bring joy** - This phrase means to make someone feel happy or satisfied. Although winning a race can bring joy, this phrase is not specifically equivalent to "To breast the tape".(खुशी लाना). 

43:T66d,

The correct answer is** 'Option 4'.**</p&g
